title: Stork Delivers Jelly Water Bottle
description: A stork carries a soft-body water bottle across a sky scene. The user must click to squeeze, stretch, and deform the gelatinous water bottle mid-flight, adjusting its wobble frequency, damping, and elasticity through a multi-step calibration panel to safely land it on a target platform without it bursting.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements an interactive soft-body water bottle delivery scene. Load stork.glb and WaterBottle.glb using GLTFLoader from the paths provided. Scene setup: Use a gradient sky background (light blue to white). Place a PerspectiveCamera at (0, 3, 8) looking at origin. Add ambient light (intensity 0.6) and a directional light from (5, 10, 5) with shadows enabled. The stork model should fly in a gentle sine-wave path across the scene at y=4, with its wings gently animated. Beneath the stork, attach the WaterBottle model via a soft tether. Implement a custom vertex-based soft-body simulation on the water bottle mesh: duplicate its geometry positions into a spring-mass particle system where each vertex acts as a mass point connected to neighbors by spring constraints. Apply gravity, spring forces, and velocity damping each frame to deform the bottle geometry in real time, updating normals. Interactions (6-10 steps with validation): Step 1: User clicks a Start button to begin the flight. Step 2: User drags a Stiffness slider (range 0.1-2.0) to set spring constant k; validate k is within range. Step 3: User drags a Damping slider (range 0.01-0.5); validate value. Step 4: User clicks the bottle to apply a squeeze impulse that visibly deforms it inward; validate deformation magnitude exceeds a threshold. Step 5: User drags a Wobble Frequency slider (0.5-5.0 Hz) controlling an oscillating external force on the bottle; validate range. Step 6: User clicks a Drop button to release the tether; the bottle must free-fall with soft-body physics toward a circular landing platform at y=0. Step 7: User presses Space to apply an air-brake damping burst mid-fall; validate it was pressed before impact. Step 8: On landing, compute max vertex displacement from rest shape. If under a burst threshold, display success with confetti particles; otherwise show a burst animation. Display a parameter summary panel showing all chosen values and result. Use OrbitControls for camera. Render at 60fps with requestAnimationFrame. All UI controls should be HTML overlays styled with semi-transparent dark panels and white text.
